text: Graphicle maps your repository into a code graph, remembers your project's docs, decisions and past agent sessions, and gives your coding agent cited excerpts from both: the exact files and lines. It runs on your machine: no API key needed, no account, no telemetry . Works with Claude Code · Cursor · Codex · VS Code · Claude Desktop · any MCP client Quick start · How it works · Benchmarks · Docs · Coming from Graphify? · Discussions brew install graphicle-ai/tap/graphicle cd your-repo graphicle setup No Homebrew? curl -fsSL https://github.com/graphicle-ai/graphicle/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh · Release archives · Other ways to install Windows: no native build yet; under WSL2 the Linux install should work (not yet tested). Native Windows support is planned. graphicle setup indexes the repository, builds its code graph and connects the coding agents it finds. It also turns on session capture, points Claude Code's searches to the code graph first, adds a short section to AGENTS.md and installs Git hooks that keep the project current. It lists every file it changes and backs each one up first; graphicle disconnect undoes it all. Then ask your agent to "use graphicle to find where failed requests are retried" , or ask from the terminal: $ graphicle ask " where is tax added to prices? " Evidence for "where is tax added to prices?" 4 excerpts · 598 of 3,000 tokens [1] shop/pricing.py:1-7 price_with_tax() """Prices and tax.""" TAX_RATE = 0.2 def price_with_tax(price): """A price with the sales tax added.""" return round(price * (1 + TAX_RATE), 2) Real output, cut after the first excerpt. With no model configured, ask shows the evidence; graphicle config set model anthropic (or openai , ollama ) adds written answers. Paste this into Claude Code, Codex or Cursor: Install Graphicle with `brew install graphicle-ai/tap/graphicle` (or, without Homebrew, `curl -fsSL https://github.com/graphicle-ai/graphicle/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh`), then run `graphicle setup --yes` in this repository and list every file it changed. Start here You want to Run Give your coding agent the code graph and your project's memory graphicle setup in the repository Ask a question from the terminal graphicle ask "how are failed requests retried?" Browse the graph, the sources and the memory graphicle open See what a change to a symbol touches graphicle graph extract . --code-only , then graphicle graph affected "retry()" Check that everything works graphicle doctor Undo everything setup did graphicle disconnect Move from Graphify, or run a server for a team Moving from Graphify · Team server Why Graphicle Native and fast. One Rust program. On Kubernetes (31k files), the 0.1.0 engine ran a code-only extract in 3 min 18 s, against 26 min 38 s for Graphify 0.9.88, and built the same graph (one exploratory run each, one Linux host, the same 16 CPUs, 8 workers). Context, not re-reading. Your agent asks Graphicle and gets the relevant code, docs and decisions as cited excerpts, within a token budget. Answers you can check. Every excerpt names its file and lines. Memories an agent proposes wait for your approval. One program, not a stack. The code graph, the memory, one MCP server, the web app and the command line come in one install, with one SQLite file. No Python, Docker or database server. Local and private. No account and no telemetry. Nothing leaves your machine unless you ask. graphicle setup connects every client it finds over MCP. Each file is backed up once as <file>.graphicle-bak , and graphicle disconnect removes what it added. Speed. The chart above: Kubernetes (31k files), the 0.1.0 engine (a Linux test build of the release source) against Graphify 0.9.88, one exploratory run each, both building the same graph ( Kubernetes run ). Earlier, on Django, a pre-release build ran a code-only extract in 7.5 s against 72.8 s for Graphify 0.9.77 (medians of five alternating runs, one shared Linux host, 8 workers), both building the same graph ( the 8 October record ). Memory. In a comparison with seven memory systems, registered before any answer was scored and run with one open model as every system's reader and judge, a pre-release build of Graphicle trails none on three development sets. Every score, with its method and caveats . No, for most of it. The code graph (with --code-only ), sync, context , the MCP server, session capture and the app work without one. A model writes the answers of graphicle ask , proposes memories from sources and reads documents and images in a full graphicle graph extract . Local models through Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible server work ( configuration ). The code-graph engine is a Rust port of Graphify, kept in step with Graphify's releases and credited in its file headers and in NOTICE . The parity checks name the release it follows. The memory, the memory tools, the app and session capture are not part of Graphify. Coming from Graphify? graphicle setup offers to switch a repository, backs up each file and never deletes graphify-out/ ( Moving from Graphify ). By default a project can hold up to 100,000 text files and 1 GiB of text; you can raise both (see Limits in docs/configuration.md ). A very large file is analysed in part or kept as searchable text instead of stopping a sync. Graphicle is free and open source under Apache-2.0, for individuals and teams alike. A commercial edition for teams is in private preview. To talk to us, start a discussion: https://github.com/graphicle-ai/graphicle/discussions , or chat with us on Discord . Graphicle is Apache-2.0: free to use, change and ship, commercially too. Third-party parts keep their own licences, listed in NOTICE . More answers: FAQ · Troubleshooting · or run graphicle doctor .
